# WOOW CAN (woow_can)

> Home Assistant integration for CAN / CAN FD buses on SocketCAN interfaces (can0 / can1 on a Raspberry Pi
> with a CAN HAT, or a virtual vcan0). It shows the bus per ID and in time order, estimates bus load, sends
> frames once or periodically and records candump log files. Everything people do in its panel, an AI agent
> can do through Home Assistant services; people review the agent's work in the panel's Activity tab.

## Connecting

- ha-mcp: call the services with `ha_call_service` (domain `woow_can`). Always pass `return_response: true`:
  read services refuse calls without it, and change services only return their result with it.
- Home Assistant's MCP server (mcp_server, admin): the same services are tools of the LLM API "WOOW CAN".
- Errors are readable messages: an unknown interface lists the existing ones; bad input names the field.
- Sending and settings changes (send, save_periodic, control_periodic, capture, clear_monitor) need an admin.

## Workflow

1. `describe` — what the integration does, the frame notation, the workflow, and the interfaces with health.
2. `list_interfaces` — state (`error_active` = healthy, `error_passive` with TEC >= 128 usually means no other
   node acknowledges: wiring, termination or bitrate), bus load, frames per second, drops, last error frame.
3. `get_monitor` {interface, ids} — one row per CAN ID and direction: count, rate_hz, period_ms, latest data,
   data_changes. `direction` is "tx" only for frames WOOW CAN sent; `from_this_host` marks frames other
   programs on this host sent. To find which frame an action produces: call get_monitor, ask a person to
   operate the equipment, call it again and compare data and data_changes.
4. `get_trace` {interface, ids, direction, seconds, limit, before} — frames in time order, newest first, e.g.
   a request and its reply. Page back with `before` = the previous call's `next_before`.
5. `send` {interface, frame, wait_id, wait_ms, note} — one frame; with wait_id the first frame with that ID is
   returned as `reply`. Interfaces in listen-only mode refuse to send. On a vehicle, machine or battery bus
   only send a frame the user asked for.
6. `save_periodic` {interface, frame, period_ms, count, name, start, note} / `control_periodic`
   {item, action: start|stop|delete} — frames sent every period_ms (>= 10 ms). All stop when Home Assistant
   restarts.
7. `capture` {interface, action: start|stop} and `list_captures` — candump log files under
   `<config>/woow_can/captures`.
8. `get_activity` — what changed, by whom, why. Give every send and change a short `note`.

## Devices: signals as entities

- Known equipment: `list_templates`, then `create_from_template` {template, interface, name, params}.
  Templates: `bms_lv_0x35x` (48 V batteries on 0x351-0x35F; groups pylon / sma / victron / inverter are
  detected from traffic when not given), `j1939_engine_vehicle` and `j1939_dm1` (params source_address, hex,
  empty = any), `nmea2000_dc` (instance, source_address), `canopen_node_monitor` (node_id, heartbeat_ms).
- `list_devices` / `get_device` show current values, whether each message is still arriving, entity ids.
- DBC files: `import_dbc` {name, content, attach}, `attach_dbc`, `create_from_dbc` {dbc, interface, messages}.
- Unknown frames: find the ID with get_monitor (data_changes while a person operates the equipment), try a
  field with `test_signal` {interface, can_id, start, length, byte_order, signed, factor, offset}, then
  `save_device` with a definition (the shape is in `describe` -> device_definition and in `get_device`).
- `set_signal` {device, message, signal, adopted, min_interval, tolerance, timeout} adopts a signal as an
  entity or tunes it. `decode_frame` {interface, frame} shows what the definitions make of one frame.

Interfaces can be named by config entry id, name (`CAN0`) or interface (`can0`).

## Notation

- Frames (cansend): `123#11223344` (11-bit ID: 1-3 hex digits), `18FF50E5#0102` (29-bit: more digits),
  `123#R` (remote frame), `456##1AABBCC` (CAN FD; the digit after `##` holds the flags, 1 = bit rate switch).
- ID lists (`ids`, the event filter): `123, 18FF50E5, 7E0/7F0, 100-1FF` — exact IDs, ID/mask, ranges; `*` = all.
- Data in results is hex with spaces (`"14 02 74 0E"`), byte 0 first.

## Events

`woow_can_frame` fires for received frames whose ID is in the interface's "IDs that fire events" option
(empty by default): entry_id, name, interface, frame, id, id_hex, data, length, extended, fd, brs, rtr.

## Safety

- Listen-only interfaces never acknowledge or send.
- Never send frames that control engines, drives or batteries (J1939 TSC1, CANopen NMT reset, enabling a
  drive) or clear fault codes (OBD-II mode 04, J1939 DM11) unless the user asked for exactly that.
- Every send made through the services is in the activity log with the user and the note.
